title: The dance of the forces
blurb: Why most things on a chart of mass and size fall on one diagonal: electromagnetism against gravity, then the strong force and fusion, then the weak force, from a stick to a neutron star, and the strangest of objects, a black hole.

segments.from: But the speed of light works

_note: The forces Short from the second take (rec75, 2026-11-18): its own opening, recorded for it ('If you try to map every single thing that exists in a chart of mass and size…', the author at 3:04: 'now I'm going to rerecord this, but only for the intro of the dance of forces'), then from 'everything in our universe is a delicate dance' to 'That's when the strangest of objects is born, a black hole' (the author at 13:10: 'so that's where the short ends'). Every simulation kept (the author, 2026-11-18: 'Dont cut any of the sim animations from the short, it's why the short is special'): the chemical bonds, the giant planets' atoms crushed, fusion, the weak force and the neutrons packed shoulder to shoulder. Still left out: gravity against electromagnetism and the round worlds, 'Get massive enough…', the small stars' end, the heavy elements; escape velocity comes in on '…escape velocity, the speed you need to win the tug of war against an object's gravity'.
